newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares rise on stimulus of mining sector.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares rise on stimulus of mining sector.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange rose Tuesday for the second session this week due to healthy investor interest in mining stocks, brokers said.
They predicted Wednesday's session would be stable with some technical corrections after the rises.
The General Index rose 1.19 percent to 1,597.53 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index gained 1.37 percent to 2,290.12.

"The market was strong today due to the influence of the mining sector which shows strength due to the good international prices of metals, especially zinc," said Flavio Campos, of Finanval brokerage.
In a total of 2,258 trades, volume was estimated at an improved 47.6 million soles ($18 million) as 53 stocks rose, 25 were stable and 21 fell.
Biggest advancers included financial holding Credicorp, up 5.22 percent to $23.20, and miners Atacocha, up 4.44 percent to 0.94 sol and Buenaventura, up 4.18 percent to 21.20 soles.
Brokers said Buenaventura was continuing to gain from its recent judicial victory against former French partner BRGM for a 24.7 percent stake in the Yauricocha gold mine.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru also gained 1.20 percent to 5.89 soles on 2.4 million shares or 30 percent of total market volume.

"Today we saw a show of investor confidence and a marked interest for taking positions in leaders for the medium- and long-term," said Manuel Torres, of Finvest brokerage. "Also there were speculative purchases of some industrial stocks."
